## Question and hypothesis

Can the existing tracking analysis support a reproducible comparison of
multi-electron reconstruction models? The working hypothesis is that inspecting
one- and two-electron events will reveal spatial failure modes worth measuring
on a held-out sample. This report audits the method; quantitative evaluation is
pending.

code selects the run directory
`/scratch/degraw/imaging/multi_electron_v4/checkpoints/2026-06-25/07-41-12`
and reads `predict.root` and `config.yaml` from that directory.

## Existing analysis method

The notebook derives spatial voxel edges and time bounds from the saved
configuration. It sets `WEIGHT_FIELD = "n_photons"` with a threshold of 500
photons; an alternative deposited-energy mode uses 0.1 MeV. Predicted points
are selected using their `energy` field, so its interpretation must be checked
against the training configuration before comparing weight modes.

Event selection scans in input order, aiming to collect three events with one
primary electron vertex and two with two primary electron vertices (PDG 11).
These are illustrative examples, not a random performance sample. If either
group is too small, the notebook can display fewer than five events.

The figures show predicted points, original truth tracks, and voxelized truth
and predictions. The notebook exports interactive displays to `docs/event_*.html`
and updates `docs/index.html`. Those files remain the existing event gallery;
this journal does not rerun or regenerate them.

## Results and limitations

No new training, prediction, or notebook execution was performed for this audit.
No numerical performance improvement is established. Existing interactive HTML
files are present, but their generating run and freshness were not verified.

The selected events can help diagnose topology and localization errors. They
cannot establish aggregate accuracy, uncertainty, or superiority to a baseline.
The saved run artifacts are required to complete provenance and confirm the
meaning and units of the predicted `energy` field.

## Decision and next experiment

Retain the event displays as qualitative diagnostics. Before making a model
comparison, recover the saved run provenance and define a fixed held-out event
manifest shared by the baseline and candidate. Report event counts by electron
multiplicity, an agreed spatial reconstruction metric with units, and uncertainty
on the comparison. Record failures as well as representative event displays.
